title: Synthesis and Structural Characterization of Several Ytterbium Bis(trimethylsilyl)amides Including Base-free [Yb{N(SiMe3)2}2(μ-Cl)]2 – A Coordinatively Unsaturated Complex with Additional Agostic Yb···(H3C–Si) Interactions

synthesis.procedure: Under argon using modified Schlenk techniques, a solution of NaN(SiMe3)2 (12.18 g, 66.4 mmol) in 200 mL THF was added at 0 °C to a stirred suspension of YbCl3 (9.55 g, 34.2 mmol) in 50 mL THF. Stirring was continued overnight and the solvent was removed under reduced pressure. The remaining solid was treated with toluene, filtered, and the amber solution concentrated to ca. 150 mL. Cooling at −10 °C first deposited pale yellow needles of 4. The mother liquor was evaporated and the residue extracted into n-pentane; concentration and storage at 0 °C gave yellow crystals of 1 as a mixture of crystalline forms 1a and 1b, contaminated with a small amount (<5%) of cluster 2.
synthesis.temperature: addition at 0 °C; crystallization at 0 °C after −10 °C isolation of 4
synthesis.vessel_or_method: modified Schlenk techniques under purified argon
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solvent removed under reduced pressure; toluene extraction and filtration; n-pentane extraction; concentration to incipient crystallization and storage at 0 °C

synthesis.procedure: Cluster 2 formed as a minor product (<5%) in the same reaction used to prepare 1 and 4: NaN(SiMe3)2 (12.18 g, 66.4 mmol) in 200 mL THF was added at 0 °C to YbCl3 (9.55 g, 34.2 mmol) in 50 mL THF, stirred overnight, then worked up via toluene and n-pentane. Isolated crystals of 1 were shown by microscopy, Raman spectroscopy and X-ray cell determination to contain a small amount of 2. The oxide source is attributed to THF/base chemistry rather than oxychloride impurity in YbCl3.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: obtained as a minor crystalline contaminant of 1 after toluene/n-pentane workup

synthesis.procedure: A solution of [Yb{N(SiMe3)2}2(μ-Cl)(thf)] (3.74 g, 6.6 mmol) in n-heptane (ca. 30 mL) was heated to 90 °C for 4 h, with intermittent exposure to dynamic vacuum. The cloudy solution was filtered and the yellow filtrate stored at −20 °C. After 2 days pale yellow needles of 4 and yellow prisms of 1a deposited; after 5 months a small amount of orange plates of 3 was obtained and separated mechanically from 1a and 4.
synthesis.time: heated 4 hours; crystals of 3 after 5 months at −20 °C

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration of cloudy solution; storage at −20 °C; mechanical separation of orange plates from 1a and 4

synthesis.procedure: Obtained as a major co-product of the NaN(SiMe3)2/YbCl3 reaction used for 1. After toluene workup, cooling the concentrated solution at −10 °C gave pale yellow needles of 4 (3.36 g, 15%). Further workup of the remaining solution afforded an additional batch of 4 (2.68 g, 12%) purified by sublimation at 10^−3 mbar. Heating 1 to 200 °C under vacuum also produced 4 by desolvation/disproportionation.
synthesis.temperature: addition at 0 °C; crystallization at −10 °C; sublimation used for purification
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk synthesis followed by crystallization and sublimation at 10^−3 mbar
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: toluene extraction; cooling at −10 °C; additional crop after workup of mother liquor; purification by sublimation
synthesis.yield: 3.36 g (15%) plus further 2.68 g (12%); total ca. 25%

synthesis.procedure: First obtained by uncontrolled air oxidation of Yb{N(SiMe3)2}2(thf)2; deliberately prepared by adding dry dioxygen (14 mL, 0.63 mmol) at −60 °C via syringe to an orange solution of Yb{N(SiMe3)2}2(thf)2 (0.73 g, 1.14 mmol) in 20 mL n-pentane. The solution decolorized and became cloudy. After filtration the filtrate was concentrated to ca. 5 mL and cooled at −60 °C to give colorless crystals of 5 suitable for X-ray diffraction.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: syringe addition of dry O2 under argon Schlenk conditions
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration of cloudy mixture; concentration to ca. 5 mL; cooling at −60 °C
